 Assistant or Associate Professor (Research Track, Tenure Eligible) 
  
 Position: Neuroimaging Scientist, Department of Radiology, Cincinnati Children's Hospital Medical Center
  
 The Department of Radiology at Cincinnati Children's Hospital Medical Center (CCHMC) seeks an outstanding PhD scientist for a tenure-eligible faculty position at the Assistant or Associate Professor level. We are conducting an open search for a highly accomplished investigator with expertise in advanced neuroimaging and a demonstrated record of impactful scholarship, multidisciplinary collaboration, and extramural research funding (or strong potential to obtain sustained funding).
  
 The successful candidate will join the Division of Radiology Research in the Department of Radology and will contribute to expanding and advancing CCHMC's neuroimaging research enterprise. This recruitment aligns with institutional priorities in neuroscience, brain development, neurodevelopmental disorders, and mental and behavioral health, while strengthening the Department's leadership in innovative imaging science and translational research.
  
 Position Responsibilities 
 The successful candidate will:
 Develop and maintain an independent, nationally recognized, externally funded research program in neuroimaging.
 Lead innovative investigations focused on brain development, physiology, pathophysiology, and/or brain function in health and/or disease.
 Advance state-of-the-art neuroimaging acquisition and/or analysis methods, including structural, functional, diffusion, and quantitative imaging approaches.
 Collaborate with multidisciplinary investigators across Cincinnati Children's and external partner institutions.
 Contribute to translational research efforts designed to improve understanding of neurological and neurodevelopmental diseases and support personalized pediatric care.
 Mentor trainees, research staff, graduate students, fellows, and junior investigators.
 Participate in departmental and institutional service activities.
 Contribute to educational programs within the Department of Radiology and the broader academic community.
  
 Required Qualifications 
 PhD in Biomedical Engineering, Neuroscience, Medical Physics, Imaging Science, Computer Science, Psychology, Chemistry, or a related quantitative or biomedical discipline.
 Established expertise in advanced neuroimaging methods and/or analysis.
 Publication record in peer-reviewed scientific journals.
 Demonstrated success in obtaining extramural research funding or strong potential to secure independent funding.
 Experience working within multidisciplinary research teams.
 Excellent communication and mentoring skills.
  
 Preferred Qualifications 
 Expertise in one or more advanced neuroimaging modalities, including: Functional MRI (fMRI)
 Diffusion Tensor Imaging (DTI) and advanced diffusion methods
 Quantitative MRI
 Neuroimage analysis, machine learning, or computational neuroscience
 Other relevant modalities / techniques
 
 Experience with pediatric imaging research.
 Interest in translational studies bridging imaging science and clinical neuroscience.
 Experience developing novel acquisition, processing, or quantitative imaging methodologies
  
 Research Environment 
 Cincinnati Children's is one of the leading pediatric research institutions in the United States and provides an exceptional environment for collaborative neuroimaging research. The successful candidate will have opportunities to collaborate with faculty across the Department of Radiology, including neuroradiology, imaging physics, and quantitative imaging programs, as well as investigators throughout the institution and at the University of Cincinnati.
  
 Potential collaborators include faculty within Radiology, Neonatology, Neurology, Neurosurgery, Mental and Behavioral Health, Rehabilitation Medicine, Biostatistics and Epidemiology, the Center for Brain Development and Injury (CBDI), General & Community Pediatrics, and other research programs focused on brain development and neurodevelopmental disorders.
  
 Position Details 
 Position: Assistant or Associate Professor
 Track: Research Track, Tenure Eligible
 Degree Required: PhD
 FTE: 1.0
 Effort Distribution (approximate and negotiable): Research: 90%
 Administration: 5%
 Teaching: 5%
 Clinical: 0%
 
 Anticipated Start Date: July 1, 2027
 Initial Support: Departmental start-up support with expectation of transition to extramural funding
 Division Director: Kim Cecil, PhD
 Radiologist-in-Chief: Andrew Trout, MD
  
 Application Process 
 Interested candidates should submit:
 Curriculum vitae
 Cover letter describing research interests and future research plans
 Statement of research accomplishments and funding history
 Contact information for three references
  
 For questions regarding this opportunity, please contact:
 Jonathan R. Dillman, MD, MSc
 Associate Chief, Research
 Department of Radiology
 Jonathan.dillman@cchmc.org 
 (or Kelsey Hogan, administrative assistant [kelsey.hogan@cchmc.org])
